description:
FILED s452ab (Opus, round 11 agent AB) while fixing #720.  THE RESIDUE OF
THAT TASK, with the fixes MEASURED AND BACKED OUT -- read this before
retrying either of them as written.

#720 fixed the SLICE half: a slice is a SUBSCRIPTED dereference and perl
vivifies the base of one, so the four slice emitters now lower their
container in lvalue context (`Pl::ExprToCL::_slice_base_form`) and
`p-cast-%` gained the autovivification arm its `p-cast-@` twin already had.
Three sibling shapes are still WRONG, and each has a one- or two-line fix
that was tried, measured and reverted because it widens further than #720's
bar and needs a sweep leg of its own.

(a) `${ ELEM }[i] = V` / `${ ELEM }{k} = V` WRITES NOWHERE (silent wrong):
        my %e; ${ $e{k} }[0] = 3;   perl: $e{k} is ARRAY [3];  PCL: absent
        my %f; ${ $f{k} }{z} = 4;   perl: $f{k} is HASH  [z=4]; PCL: absent
    The arrow spelling (`$e{k}->[0] = 3`) and the chain (`$x->{a}{b} = 1`)
    are RIGHT -- they lower to `(setf p-aref)` / `(setf p-gethash)`, which
    vivify through the element.  Only `p-aref-deref` / `p-gethash-deref` as
    a p-setf PLACE fail: their writers go through `p-ensure-arrayref` /
    `p-ensure-hashref`, which need the element's BOX, and the emitter hands
    them the throwaway box `p-gethash` returns for a missing key.
    THE FIX TRIED: generate the base of `gen_array_ref_access_form` /
    `gen_hash_ref_access_form` through `_slice_base_form` (i.e. in lvalue
    context), exactly as the slice bases now do.  It WORKS (all five probe
    shapes matched perl).  WHY IT WAS BACKED OUT: `lvalue_context` is also
    what the child's own accessor choice reads, so a NESTED `p-aref-deref`
    base flips to the live-box `p-aref-deref-box` -- 4 corpus files moved
    (grep.t, list.t, ref.t, postfixderef.t), a snapshot-to-live-box widening
    on read paths that needs its own full sweep.

(b) `%{ ELEM } = (a=>1)` IS A SILENT NO-OP where `@{ ELEM } = (5,6)` works:
        my %z; %{ $z{k} } = (a=>1);  perl: HASH [a=1];  PCL: absent
    Cause: `p-cast-%`'s operand is NOT lowered in lvalue context, while
    `p-cast-@`'s is (`$needs_lvalue = ($op eq '@')` in ExprToCL's cast
    emitter).  THE FIX TRIED: add `%` to that test.  It WORKS.  WHY IT WAS
    BACKED OUT: an lvalue accessor VIVIFIES, and a BARE rvalue deref must
    not -- perl leaves the key absent for `keys %{ $h{k} }` (probed) -- and
    the emission A/B over 1030 files turned 15 real READ sites in
    Test2/Test::Builder/Text::CSV_PP into vivifications (10 Test-Simple
    files + Text::CSV_PP + delete.t + local.t).  The `@` twin has carried
    that same over-vivification since forever; extending it is a behaviour
    change on the harness's own modules and needs a sweep leg.
    NOTE the honest shape of the whole family: PCL over-vivifies a BARE
    rvalue deref (`keys @{ $h{k} }`, `scalar @{ $h{k} }` -- perl: key
    absent, PCL: present) because the cast emitter cannot tell lvalue from
    rvalue.  A real fix would give the cast the context, which is the
    principled version of both (a) and (b).

(c) `%{ $u }{'x'}` with a RAW-SLOT scalar does not vivify: `my $u3; my @g =
    %{ $u3 }{"x"}` leaves $u3 undef (perl: HASH).  VarAnnotator marked $u3
    unboxable, so the `let` binds `(p-undef)` and `p-cast-%`'s arm -- which
    tests `(p-box-p val)` -- cannot fire.  The ELEMENT-based spelling
    (`%{ $a{k} }{"x"}`) is right, and so is every write-through case (a
    write makes VarAnnotator keep the box).

BAR for whoever takes this: the probe files are reproduced above; run all
three groups vs perl in BOTH directions, plus the emission A/B over the four
populations AND a full sweep leg (both (a) and (b) move read paths in the
harness's own modules).  Guard rows beside the #720 family in
Pl/t/aassign-01.t.
subject: #720 residue: ${ELEM}[i] writes nowhere, %{ELEM}=(...) is a no-op, and the cast emitter over-vivifies a bare rvalue deref (fixes measured and backed out)
